question.prompt:
What is the area of the region in the coordinate plane defined by

\[ ||x|-1|+||y|-1|\le 1? \]

solutions.title: Find one quadrant and reflect
solutions.explanation:
Changing the sign of either coordinate leaves the inequality unchanged, so we can find the area in the first quadrant and multiply by four.

For \(x,y\ge0\), the condition becomes
\[
|x-1|+|y-1|\le1.
\]
The lines \(x=1\) and \(y=1\) split this region into four pieces. In each piece, let \(a=|x-1|\) and \(b=|y-1|\), the horizontal and vertical distances from \((1,1)\). The condition is
\[
a\ge0,\qquad b\ge0,\qquad a+b\le1.
\]
Thus each piece is a right triangle with perpendicular legs of length \(1\), so its area is \(\tfrac12\). The four choices of direction from \((1,1)\) give four congruent triangles, all within the first quadrant because \(a,b\le1\). Together they form the diamond with vertices
\[
(0,1),\ (1,0),\ (2,1),\ (1,2),
\]
whose area is \(4\cdot\tfrac12=2\).

Reflecting across the coordinate axes gives four copies with disjoint interiors. Their shared boundary points contribute no area, so the total is
\[
\boxed{4\cdot2=8},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).

solutions.title: Take half of each unit square
solutions.explanation:
The absolute-value expression is linear on each unit interval between \(-2\) and \(2\), so a unit grid makes the area easy to calculate.

Write \(f(t)=\bigl||t|-1\bigr|\). Since both terms in \(f(x)+f(y)\le1\) are nonnegative, each is at most \(1\). Consequently \(|x|,|y|\le2\), and the region lies in the square \([-2,2]\times[-2,2]\).

Removing the absolute values on each interval gives

| Interval for \(t\) | \(f(t)\) |
|---|---|
| \([-2,-1]\) | \(-t-1\) |
| \([-1,0]\) | \(t+1\) |
| \([0,1]\) | \(1-t\) |
| \([1,2]\) | \(t-1\) |

On every listed interval, \(f(t)\) is the distance from the endpoint where its value is \(0\).

The integer grid divides the bounding square into \(16\) unit squares. In each one, there is exactly one corner where both \(f(x)\) and \(f(y)\) vanish. Let \(a,b\) be the horizontal and vertical distances from that corner. The table gives \(f(x)=a\) and \(f(y)=b\), so the included portion satisfies \(a+b\le1\). This is a right triangle with legs \(1\), occupying half the unit square.

The unit squares cover every possible point and overlap only along edges. Hence the total area is
\[
\boxed{16\cdot\frac12=8},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
